recent_articles.title: Rare 'intensive' revision in Bihar four months before polls - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** has ordered a special summary revision of electoral rolls in Bihar, marking a departure from its usual practice.  This revision differs from previous intensive revisions by utilizing the 2002-03 electoral roll as a base and incorporating a new pre-printed enumeration form for house-to-house verification. The ECI's decision to conduct this revision ahead of the assembly elections in October 2025 is unusual, as it has rarely ordered full state-wide intensive revisions so far out from the scheduled polls.  This move follows a pattern of the ECI conducting 'intensive' revision in specific areas of states based on various factors like population changes or electoral irregularities.

recent_articles.title: Govt. plans security protocol for fishing harbours under CISF oversight - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF)** will oversee the security of around 1,200 fishing harbours and landing sites across India as part of a plan to strengthen the country's coastline. The **Union Home Ministry** aims to implement this framework after assigning CISF personnel to secure 250 seaports. This move follows guidelines issued by the **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** in 2023, and is intended to provide a uniform security template for all coastal areas.  The government's objective is to ensure the safety of fisherfolk and prevent potential threats like those seen during the 26/11 Mumbai attacks.

recent_articles.title: Monsoon to reach Kerala on May 26, says IMD - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** predicts the southwest monsoon will advance into Kerala on May 26, a day earlier than its usual June 1 arrival.  While this year's monsoon onset is anticipated to be early, there are concerns about below-normal rainfall. The IMD has historically been accurate in predicting the monsoon's arrival over Kerala, with only one exception in 2015. **M. Ravichandran**, Secretary of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, stated that after the monsoon onset, a period of heavy rain is expected for the next five days.  The IMD has warned of potential drought impacts due to reduced rainfall and the ongoing El Nino phenomenon.

recent_articles.title: Nicobarese oppose proposal for three wildlife sanctuaries - The Hindu
recent_articles.sentiment_target: Tribal Council of Little and Great Nicobar
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union government** notified three wildlife sanctuaries in the Little Nicobar, Menchal, and Meroe islands in 2022, despite concerns from the **Tribal Council of Little and Great Nicobar** that the process was not conducted with proper consultation. The council argues that these islands are culturally and spiritually significant to them and their traditional practices should be respected.  Congress leader and former Environment Minister **Jairam Ramesh** has written to Tribal Affairs Minister **Jual Oram**, urging him to intervene and withdraw clearances granted under the Forest Rights Act for the Great Nicobar Island project, citing violations of the law. The **Tribal Council** has consistently objected to the sanctuaries' declaration, arguing that it encroaches on their pre-existing rights and will negatively impact their livelihoods.  The Calcutta High Court has dismissed preliminary objections raised by the government in relation to the Forest Rights Act violation allegations.

recent_articles.title: World Deadliest Snakes: King Cobra Capitals: 10 countries where the world’s deadliest snake thrives | World News - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **King cobras**, the world's longest venomous snake, inhabit forests and wetlands across South and Southeast Asia.  Top countries with significant populations include India, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Nepal, Vietnam, Cambodia, and China. These countries support diverse king cobra habitats, which are threatened by habitat loss, deforestation, and poaching.  Conservation efforts focus on protecting forest corridors and educating communities about safe coexistence with these fascinating creatures.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Gram Sabhas that gave nod to Nicobar project did not have mandatory 50% quorum - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** administration claims to have achieved the required quorum for the Great Nicobar Island project, despite attendance figures ranging from 2% to 15% of the population. The administration argues that this constitutes proper quorum under the Forest Rights Act (FRA) rules. However, petitions before the Calcutta High Court challenge the process, alleging violations and arguing that the Tribal Council should have been consulted instead of the Gram Sabhas.  The Central government has also requested time to demonstrate consent from tribal people.

recent_articles.title: Tallest underwater human stack formed; Andaman sets two Guinness World Records in 2 days - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** officials achieved two Guinness World Records on May 2nd and 3rd, 2026.  The first record involved a 22.3-meter underwater human stack formed by fourteen people, including Lieutenant-Governor D.K. Joshi. The second record was the unfurling of the world's largest underwater national flag. These achievements are part of an initiative to promote the islands as a premier global diving destination.  Both records are expected to draw attention and boost tourism.

recent_articles.title: Scuba team unfurls mega national flag beneath deep sea, enters into Guinness World Records - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sharath R. Ashok**, a Bengaluru-based adventure sports professional, led a team of 200 scuba divers in successfully unfurling a massive national flag beneath the sea at Swaraj Dweep in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The Guinness World Records recognized this extraordinary feat, with **Lieutenant Governor Admiral D.K. Joshi** presenting the team with an official certificate.  The mission was organized by the **Andaman and Nicobar administration** and the **Indian defense forces**, showcasing Mr. Ashok's diverse training in adventure sports that enabled him to successfully complete the underwater challenge.

recent_articles.title: Andaman sets Guinness World Record by unfurling largest underwater national flag - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Andaman and Nicobar** administration set a new Guinness World Record by unfurling the world's largest underwater national flag at Radhanagar beach. The massive Tricolour, measuring approximately 60 by 40 metres, was deployed beneath the sea in a complex operation involving multiple agencies and trained divers. **Lieutenant Governor D.K. Joshi**, **Chief Secretary Chandra Bhushan Kumar**, and **Director General of Police HS Dhaliwal** witnessed the event.  Personnel from various agencies collaborated to execute the intricate underwater unfurling, with Guinness World Records adjudicator **Rishi Nath** formally confirming the achievement.

recent_articles.title: Rahul Gandhi plans Great Nicobar visit, clearance awaited - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the Opposition, began a three-day visit to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands for a Congress convention in Port Blair.  He is scheduled to also visit Great Nicobar Island where the **Union government** plans a large infrastructure project that has raised concerns among tribal communities about displacement and loss of rights over their forests. **Manickam Tagore**, Congress in-charge of the islands, said Gandhi assured the people in Port Blair he would continue to fight for their rights in Delhi.

recent_articles.title: Rahul Gandhi on two-day visit to Andaman and Nicobar Islands from April 26 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, will visit the Andaman and Nicobar Islands from April 26 to 28.  He is expected to focus on concerns regarding the **Centre's** ₹81,000 crore Great Nicobar Holistic Development Project, which has raised environmental concerns. The project is expected to be a key topic of discussion during his visit.

recent_articles.title: Rahul Gandhi on two-day visit to Andaman and Nicobar Islands from April 26 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, will visit the Andaman and Nicobar Islands from April 26 to 28. He plans to highlight concerns about the **Centre's** ₹81,000-crore Great Nicobar Holistic Development Project, which has raised environmental concerns.  The former Congress chief is expected to travel to Great Nicobar Island during his visit.

recent_articles.title: Door-to-door visit by Census enumerators in eight States/U.T.s from April 16 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** announced the commencement of door-to-door enumeration for the first phase of the 2027 Population Census, known as the House Listing and Housing Operations (HLO). Beginning on April 16th in eight states and union territories including Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Goa, Karnataka, Lakshadweep, Mizoram, Odisha, Sikkim, and Delhi's NDMC area and Cantonment Board, enumerators will collect data for the HLO phase. This follows a 15-day self-enumeration period.

recent_articles.title: About 250 people feared missing as boat capsizes in Andaman Sea: UN | India News - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A **UNHCR** spokesperson reported that a boat carrying Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi nationals capsized in the Andaman Sea, leaving approximately 250 people missing. The incident, which occurred after the trawler departed from Teknaf in Bangladesh for Malaysia, is believed to have been caused by heavy winds, rough seas, and overcrowding.  **UNHCR** and **IOM** emphasized that the tragedy highlights the dire consequences of protracted displacement and urged the international community to provide support for both Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh and Bangladeshi host communities.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 9 States and 3 UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by **West Bengal**, with a net deletion of 83.86 lakh. The SIR phase II identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters across these states and UTs.  The consolidated electoral rolls saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

recent_articles.title: Tourism and trade: The Hindu Editorial on the Great Nicobar mega-infrastructure project - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union government**’s ₹92,000 crore mega-infrastructure project for Great Nicobar Island (GNI) is moving forward with a draft master plan outlining plans for tourism and economic development. The plan envisions building the island as a "seaside destination" and aims to create over 3.36 lakh jobs by 2055, but it has drawn criticism from indigenous groups like the Nicobarese and Shompen who oppose relocation plans and fear ecological damage.  The draft plan is open for public feedback, but its timeline remains unclear. Concerns remain about the project's impact on biodiversity, local rights, and commercial viability.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 12 States and UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which saw a significant reduction in voter numbers across nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by West Bengal with 83.86 lakh.  The revision identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters for removal. The consolidated electoral rolls across these regions saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

recent_articles.title: Voters' lists in 12 States, Union Territories shrink by over 6 crore post SIR - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced that the combined voters' list for nine states and three union territories has decreased by nearly 6.08 crore after the completion of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise on Friday, April 10, 2026. The final electoral rolls for Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Kerala, Puducherry, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Goa have been published.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Self-enumeration facility availed by 5.72 lakh households so far in first phase - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Registrar General of India (RGI)** announced that over 5.72 lakh households have utilized the self-enumeration facility during the first phase of the Census 2027. This digital initiative reflects growing participation in the census, with a special portal available for citizens in specific areas including Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Goa, Karnataka, Sikkim, Odisha, Lakshadweep, Mizoram, and Delhi's NDMC and Cantonment Board. The self-enumeration facility allows citizens to provide their details online, facilitating a faster and more convenient contribution to nation-building.

recent_articles.title: States to be pushed for ‘utility led aggregation’ to meet PM Surya Ghar targets - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)** is seeking to boost the adoption of its **PM Surya Ghar** program, which aims to provide solar energy access to one crore households by March 2027. The MNRE is encouraging states to adopt a “utility-led aggregation (ULA)” model where electricity distribution companies will pay for rooftop solar installations in eligible households.  The program has seen limited uptake but the MNRE is proposing incentives to increase participation. Despite this, India's renewable energy growth was significant in 2025-26, adding 55.3 gigawatts of non-fossil capacity, with solar power accounting for 44.6 GW.

recent_articles.title: Great Nicobar Project: Draft plan to relocate’ affected Nicobarese families creates confusion - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Andaman and Nicobar Islands administration** has released a draft plan outlining the relocation of **Nicobarese tribal communities** affected by the Great Nicobar Island (GNI) mega-infrastructure project. The plan proposes a ₹42.52-crore outlay over 24 months for housing, land development, and basic infrastructure in Rajiv Nagar and New Chingenh. However, details of where specific relocation will take place and which communities will be affected remain unclear, raising concerns among the **Tribal Council of Great and Little Nicobar**. The plan also faces scrutiny due to its lack of clarity on forest rights, with the **Nicobarese communities** alleging that their rights under the 2006 Forest Rights Act have not been properly addressed.

recent_articles.title: 55,000 households use Census self-enumeration portal on day one - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **President Droupadi Murmu**, **Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan**, **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, and **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** were among the first to use the online self-enumeration portal for the 2027 Population Census in eight States and Union Territories. The portal, which launched on April 1, 2026, allows households to provide information about their housing conditions and assets before enumerators visit.  The first phase of the census, focusing on house listing operations and housing census (HLO), will run until May 15th in these areas. Data collected through self-enumeration is confidential and will be used for evidence-based planning and policy formulation.

recent_articles.title: Strait Of Malacca China Vulnerability: Hormuz is a trailer. Malacca is China’s real nightmare — and India knows it - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Strait of Hormuz is experiencing a crisis, highlighting the vulnerability of global energy supply chains. The Strait of Malacca, a critical shipping lane connecting Asia to the world, poses an even greater threat to China's economy as it carries a significant portion of its energy imports and trade. India's strategic advantage lies in its proximity to the strait and its ability to monitor and disrupt maritime traffic through its Andaman and Nicobar Islands. The US is also concerned about Malacca's vulnerability, but India's geographic position gives it an edge over China.  China faces potential economic disruption if the Strait of Malacca experiences a crisis, as disruptions in shipping routes could lead to higher costs, delays, and supply chain vulnerabilities.

recent_articles.title: Andaman's tribal delegation meets Rahul Gandhi, raises concern over Great Nicobar project - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A delegation of tribal leaders from the Andaman and Nicobar Islands met with **Rahul Gandhi**, Congress leader, in New Delhi to express concerns about the proposed Great Nicobar Infrastructure project. The delegation emphasized the potential negative impact on the island's ecosystem and indigenous communities, urging a balanced approach that prioritizes environmental conservation and safeguards traditional rights.  **Dr. Vikrant Bhuria**, national chairman of the All India Adivasi Congress, was also present at the meeting. **Gandhi** assured the delegation that their concerns would be raised at appropriate fora and expressed his intention to visit the islands to better understand the situation.
